title: Societies' yearly parades and the Jolly Boys picnic
summary: Old benevolent societies paraded; the Jolly Boys still do, taking in members just for parade season and planning a picnic.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, in those days we even had the fairground. They would give, like these big bands would come out of the city, come here to the city, well they'd go and play at the fairgrounds, the Oddfellas, and the Knights of Piffion, and all those fellas, they'd give things. Each year those people used to parade at big parades. The Oddfellas, then the Knights of Piffion, then the Mason, well all those fellas used to parade. They don't parade no more, nothing but they also parade. But those times all those societies, and the young men, Olympians, and all them people, they were societies, but they'd parade every year. It's just a fair. We the only, the Elks, and well you might catch the scabber clubs, come around. But those clubs, they would parade yearly. Just like we do now, the Jolly Boys. Now we the only club that really parades yearly. They had the Bulls. They had the Tanami. Well all those fellas used to parade. The Hobgobblers. That's in the olden times. Every week it was a parade. But now they did. The younger fellas, he don't want to spend no money, and the older fellas had died out. So my club, they like that parade, and we got a lot of young fellas. So I'll tell you how they do now. See like this time of year, we'll all have a hundred and a hundred and fifty members. See? They want to parade. And you cannot parade unless you join the club. You got to be a member of the club to parade. So we have them coming in now like nobody's business. But after the parade, out they go. And they'll come back the next year, and then put in that membership. Stay in it maybe two months, three months. Then after that, they're going to get a dropout. We keep around forty-five, fifty, seventy-five, standing number. But they're in year in, year out. A lot of those old fellas, they don't parade, but they just stay in the club. Because they like the club. And we have a banquet, and then we have, we used to give an annual picnic, because it cost us about five hundred dollars. But it didn't cost the members nothing. The club just put that on for all the people and their families. We used to go down there to do foes. Well, the place got some beds and there's some nasty out there. Every time it'd go out there, it'd rain, and the yard wasn't sufficient. Well, this year I'm going to try to take them over the lake. Yeah, we'll try to get them over the lake this year.
